findings.title: Device limit check is racy (count then insert)
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice counts devices and then inserts in separate statements with no transaction or lock. Concurrent requests from new devices can all see count < limit and all insert, so the limit is exceeded. Across multiple Grafana instances the overshoot can be larger. The limit is not strictly enforced.

findings.title: Cache is set before the DB write, so a rejected device is cached as tagged
findings.body: tagDeviceUI sets the local cache entry before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice. When the call fails with ErrDeviceLimitReached (or a transient DB error), the key stays cached for about 29 minutes. Later requests from that device return nil with no error and are admitted as anonymous even though the limit is reached. Only the first request is rejected, so the limit is effectively bypassed. The cache entry should be set only after success.

findings.title: Tagging moved from async goroutine to the synchronous auth path
findings.body: TagDevice used to run in a goroutine with its own timeout. It now runs inline in Authenticate with the request context. Every uncached anonymous request therefore waits on a COUNT query plus a write, which adds latency. If the request context is cancelled, the tagging DB operation is aborted too. Tagging failures also now sit on the critical path.

findings.title: Count window uses two separate time.Now() calls and does not match the update window
findings.body: The count uses a window of now-30d to now+1m. The update path uses device.UpdatedAt-30d to UpdatedAt+1m. updateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached for a device that does not exist, which is the intended meaning. It returns the same error for a device that exists but is older than 30 days. This hides the real reason and adds inconsistency.

findings.title: args is mutated inside the session closure
findings.body: In updateDevice, `args = append([]interface{}{query}, args...)` runs inside the WithDbSession closure and reassigns the captured variable. If the session helper retries the closure, for example on a SQLite busy error, the query is prepended twice and the Exec call breaks. CreateOrUpdateDevice has the same pattern.
